30d.thesis: June execution, September guide, systems/support growth and positive VEL5 support a constructive base; valuation, China, recognition and cash-conversion risk require a wide low-confidence band.

90d.thesis: Process complexity, advanced packaging/HBM, systems plus service and a faster R&D engine preserve an up skew; technicals support base odds but do not solve China, valuation or conversion risk.

1y.thesis: Etch/deposition moat, installed-base economics, capital returns and long-cycle R&D/process-control investment support earnings power, with broad AI-capex, China, competition and valuation tails.

cards.unusual_signal: R&D is accelerating faster than the evidence of monetization. The $3B-plus lab-network plan, the audited $2.376B FY R&D base, and the existing global R&D-network strategy strengthen future process-development capacity. They do not yet quantify incremental bookings, tool share, software/service attachment, margin, capex, or returns. The market needs a bridge from lab throughput to customer qualification and commercial share.
cards.top_catalyst: The June-quarter evidence remains strong and quality-sensitive: $6.722B revenue, 52.0% non-GAAP gross margin, 38.4% operating margin, and $1.82 EPS. Systems revenue reached $4.250B and customer-support-related revenue/other $2.472B, so the improvement was not solely a systems-recognition spike. The September guide—$8.10B ±$0.40B, 52.0% ±1 point GM, 39.5% ±1 point operating margin, $2.15 ±$0.15 EPS—is now the central conversion test.

market_bullets: Coverage is 8/9 same-day notes; 7 names lean up or flat-to-up, while 1 lean flat-to-down or down.
Several setups still show damaged or cooling 5-bar momentum (NVDA, ARM, NET), so the regime is selective rather than a clean all-clear risk-on tape.
Semiconductor / infrastructure names still dominate the medium-term upside stack: MU, ASML, LRCX, SIMO carry the strongest multi-horizon constructive bias.
Software-edge names remain more idiosyncratic than the semis: NET is still trading as a special situation driven by credibility, ownership, and reset dynamics rather than simple sector beta.
The most common pattern is constructive 30D/90D/1Y framing paired with lower-conviction same-day calls, meaning tape damage is tactical while the business thesis often stays intact.
Calibration lessons continue to point to range-width discipline: recent misses skew more toward undershooting move magnitude than getting the broad direction wrong.
